# Lavendar Lewis

## Overview

- **Age:** Mid-forties  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034), [v2 c23 P9](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0009)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v2 c1 P46](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0046)</sub>
- **Status:** Married  <sub>[v2 c30 P29](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0029), [v2 c30 P30](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0030)</sub>
- **Origin:** Prince Edward Island  <sub>[v2 c21 P87](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0087), [v2 c22 P7](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0007)</sub>
- **Role:** Housewife  <sub>[v2 c30 P29](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0029)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Miss Lavendar  <sub>[v2 c21 P28](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0028)</sub>; Mother Lavendar  <sub>[v2 c23 P3](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0003)</sub>

## Appearance

Lavendar is a small, dainty woman with thick, snow-white hair worn in soft, becoming puffs and coils. She has a fresh, girlish, pink-cheeked face with dimples and big, expressive, wood-brown eyes containing golden glints. She possesses a sweet, tinkling voice and wears frilly, ruffled, and youthful dresses.

_Sources: [v2 c20 P4](../source/v02-c20.md#nw-v02-c20-p0004), [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045), [v2 c22 P2](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0002), [v2 c23 P9](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0009)_

## Personality

Lavendar is an imaginative, romantic, and sweet-tempered woman who retains a childlike spirit and enthusiasm into her middle age. She delights in daydreaming, playing pretend, and surrounding herself with beauty and flowers. Though proud, sensitive, and occasionally prone to sulkiness when hurt, she is deeply affectionate, hospitable, and generous. She loves young people and shares a natural, imaginative sympathy with kindred spirits.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P47](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0047), [v2 c21 P19](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0019), [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045), [v2 c21 P53](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0053), [v2 c23 P17](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0017), [v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019), [v2 c27 P23](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0023)_

## History

Lavendar Lewis grew up in Prince Edward Island and fell in love as a young woman with Stephen Irving. After a hasty quarrel caused by her pride and flirtatiousness, the engagement was broken and Stephen left for the United States, leaving her heartbroken. Lavendar chose to live a retired, quiet life at Echo Lodge, an ivy-covered stone house in Grafton. To cope with her loneliness, she created a fantasy world of pretend tea parties, echoes, and an imaginary little dream-boy. She employed a series of young maidservants whom she collectively dubbed 'Charlotta.' When Anne Shirley and Diana Barry stumbled upon Echo Lodge, they quickly became close friends with Lavendar, drawn to her imaginative nature. Later, Anne brought Stephen's son, Paul Irving, to visit her, which deeply touched Lavendar. Through Anne's intervention, Stephen Irving returned to visit Lavendar after twenty-five years apart. The two reconciled, realizing their enduring love, and were married in the garden of Echo Lodge under the honeysuckle trellis. Following their wedding, they traveled to the Pacific coast before relocating to Boston, taking Paul and Charlotta the Fourth with them, while keeping Echo Lodge as a beloved summer home.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P47](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0047), [v2 c21 P28](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0028), [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c23 P15](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0015), [v2 c23 P17](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0017), [v2 c23 P26](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0026), [v2 c28 P38](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0038), [v2 c28 P43](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0043), [v2 c28 P71](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0071), [v2 c29 P10](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0010), [v2 c30 P29](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0029)_

## Background by volume

- Daughter of a father who named her after the lavender scent he loved  <sub>[v2 c21 P83](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0083)</sub>
- Engaged in her youth to Stephen Irving, but broke it off after a petty quarrel  <sub>[v2 c22 P9](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0009), [v2 c23 P15](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0015), [v2 c23 P17](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0017)</sub>
- Lived for decades as a secluded spinster at Echo Lodge in Grafton  <sub>[v2 c1 P47](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0047), [v2 c21 P28](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0028), [v2 c22 P9](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0009)</sub>
- Hired a succession of young girls named Charlotta to keep her company  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>

## Quotes

> What is the use of being an independent old maid if you can't be silly when you want to, and when it doesn't hurt anybody?  <sub>[v2 c21 P53](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0053)</sub>

> Some are born old maids, some achieve old maidenhood, and some have old maidenhood thrust upon them.  <sub>[v2 c23 P13](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0013)</sub>

> A broken heart in real life isn't half as dreadful as it is in books. It's a good deal like a bad tooth... It takes spells of aching and gives you a sleepless night now and then, but between times it lets you enjoy life and dreams and echoes and peanut candy as if there were nothing the matter with it.  <sub>[v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019)</sub>

> Things that belong together are sure to come together. What a lot of trouble that would save some people if they only knew it.  <sub>[v2 c27 P23](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0023)</sub>
